fields.description:
## Summary

**Tier 2 (epic 5664-b797 / S5): extend the periodic sweep with the breadth practices
that carry real cost, at ZERO Gerrit Verified hot-path latency.** All new coverage
lands as scheduled-only jobs in `.github/workflows/test.yml`, which casts no
`Verified` vote (the Gerrit gate is `gerrit-verify.yaml`, invoking only the reusable
workflows — never `test.yml`). Every new job is gated
`if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`
and none is a `needs:` of a gating job, so a red sweep job is visible to the CI owner
but gates no merge — the epic's Tier-2 contract ("none of which gate a merge").

## Context / Problem

The Verified gate matrix (the shared reusable `_build-and-test.yml`) runs
`ubuntu × {3.11, 3.12, 3.13}` + `macos × 3.13` (macOS reduced to the
`platform_compat` subset). It deliberately omits — for latency — the LATEST release,
pre-release interpreters, Windows, the full macOS suite, and any check that the
DECLARED dependency floors resolve. The epic's S5 AC requires the scheduled sweep to
cover all of these, non-gating.

Verified experimentally on `origin/main` before writing this plan:
- **The committed `uv.lock` resolves cleanly on Python 3.14** (`uv sync --locked
  --python 3.14 ...` → exit 0). So the 3.14 cell installs the LOCKED dependency set —
  the exact deps the gate ships — a PURE interpreter signal, not a dep-drift canary.
- **Disentangling experiment (single-attribution):** a naïve 3.14 run that
  *re-resolved* deps (newer than the lock) showed ~140 unit failures. On **3.14 + the
  committed lock** this dropped to 0 genuine failures: ~120 were **dependency drift**
  (newer pydantic-ai/httpx, not the interpreter), ~16 a **PATH artifact** of bare
  `python -m pytest` (subprocess `ruff`/`shellcheck` off-PATH; all pass under `uv run`,
  which CI uses), and 2 this change's own gate-parity assertion (below). **Python 3.14
  has zero language/stdlib incompatibilities**, so the 3.14 cell is a legitimate
  must-pass job WHEN it uses the lock.
- A whole-project `--resolution lowest-direct` pulls unbuildable `jinja2 v2.0` via the
  FLOORLESS `ui` extra, so the lower-bound job is scoped to the properly-floored
  `core + dev + agents` set; `ui`/`reviewbot` tests self-skip via
  `importorskip("fastapi")`. Floorless extras are a separate hygiene gap (Follow-up).

## Approach

Append five scheduled-only jobs to `.github/workflows/test.yml`, each using the
already-trusted `astral-sh/setup-uv` (SHA-pinned) + `uv venv`/`uv pip install`/
`uv run --no-sync` pattern:

1. **`sweep-interpreters`** — `ubuntu` matrix over the newest stable **3.14** (real
   signal, NOT tolerated) plus pre-release **3.15** (dev) and **3.14t**
   (free-threaded), the pre-release cells non-blocking via
   `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}`. The 3.14 cell installs the
   **committed lock** (`uv sync --locked`, which resolves cleanly on 3.14) so it is a
   pure interpreter signal against the gate's exact dependency set; the pre-release
   cells predate the lock's wheel coverage, so they re-resolve latest and stay
   non-blocking. Intermediate Python (3.12/3.13) is ALREADY swept by the
   `build-and-test` reusable on this same schedule, so it needs no dedicated job.
   `fail-fast: false`.
2. **`sweep-windows`** — full default suite on `windows-latest`,
   `continue-on-error: true` (Windows is not yet a declared support target; a genuine
   incompatibility is a visible finding, not a red gate).
3. **`sweep-macos-full`** — the COMPLETE default suite (`-m "not integration and not
   external"`) on `macos-latest`, vs the gate's reduced `platform_compat` macOS
   subset.
4. **`sweep-lower-bounds`** — `uv pip install --resolution lowest-direct '.[dev,agents]'`
   on the OLDEST supported interpreter (3.11), then the unit tier, proving the
   declared floors actually resolve and work.
5. **`sweep-doc-links`** — `lycheeverse/lychee-action` over `README.md` +
   `CONTRIBUTING.md` + `docs/**/*.md`, `fail: false` + `continue-on-error: true`
   (external endpoints flake — visible, never gating). A genuinely NEW third-party
   action for this repo, so SHA-pinned
   `@e7477775783ea5526144ba13e8db5eec57747ce8  # v2.9.0` — verified via the GitHub API
   that tag `v2.9.0` resolves to exactly that commit and that `fail:` is a real input
   in that release's `action.yml`. Follows the epic's S2 supply-chain hardening.

### Affected test consumers (declared)

Two existing `tests/unit/` contract tests sweep EVERY workflow's jobs, so adding jobs
to `test.yml` must satisfy both — verified green on this change:
- `test_ci_workflow_parity.py::test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard`
  requires every CI pytest lane to carry `--timeout=<seconds>` +
  `--timeout-method=thread`. All four sweep pytest jobs (interpreters, Windows, full
  macOS, lower-bounds) run `pytest … --timeout=600 --timeout-method=thread`;
  `sweep-doc-links` runs no pytest, so it is exempt.
- `test_verify_gate_parity.py` requires every `test.yml` job to be either a Verified
  `vote.needs` or listed in `EXCLUDED_JOBS`; the five sweep jobs are added to
  `EXCLUDED_JOBS` (see the gate-parity finding above).

### Latency

Zero Gerrit Verified hot-path cost by construction: the shared reusable
`_build-and-test.yml` and the gate matrix are unmodified, and every new job is
schedule/dispatch-only in `test.yml`, which the Verified gate never invokes.

### Follow-up (out of scope, filed `discovered_from` this story)

The `ui`/`reviewbot`/`pricing` optional extras declare FLOORLESS deps (`jinja2`,
`fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `boto3`, `genai-prices`), so whole-project lowest-direct
resolution pulls unbuildable ancient versions. Adding honest floors is separate
dependency-hygiene work.

## Scope

Two files:
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` (append-only): five new scheduled-only jobs + a
  section comment.
- `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py`: add the five sweep jobs to `EXCLUDED_JOBS`
  (with justifications), so the gate-parity invariant recognises them as non-gating.

No reusable, no gate matrix, no Python/library runtime code, no dependency manifest
change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test.yml` gains scheduled-only, non-gating coverage for: newest stable Python
      (3.14), pre-release interpreters (3.15 dev + 3.14t, non-blocking), Windows,
      the full macOS suite, declared dependency lower-bound resolution, and external
      doc-link checking.
- [ ] Every new job is gated on `schedule`/`workflow_dispatch` only and is not a
      `needs:` of any merge-gating job, so none can gate a merge (the Verified gate
      —`gerrit-verify.yaml`— never invokes `test.yml`).
- [ ] Pre-release interpreter, Windows, and doc-link jobs are non-blocking
      (`continue-on-error` / `fail: false`); the 3.14 stable cell and the full macOS
      and lower-bound jobs are real signals.
- [ ] The 3.14 stable cell installs the committed lock (`uv sync --locked`) so it
      tests the interpreter against the gate's exact dependency set (pure interpreter
      signal, no dependency drift); the full unit tier passes on 3.14 + the lock.
- [ ] The five sweep jobs are listed in `EXCLUDED_JOBS` in
      `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py`, and `test_verify_gate_parity` passes.
- [ ] Every sweep pytest lane carries `--timeout=600 --timeout-method=thread`, so
      `test_ci_workflow_parity::test_every_ci_pytest_lane_has_a_per_test_hang_guard`
      passes.
- [ ] `sweep-doc-links` pins `lychee-action` to the v2.9.0 commit SHA and uses the
      confirmed `fail: false` input.
- [ ] The shared reusable `_build-and-test.yml` and the Verified gate matrix are
      unchanged, so no Gerrit Verified hot-path latency is added (the epic's central
      constraint) and the CI-parity contract test still passes.
- [ ] `make lint` (ruff + format + complexity + zizmor) and `actionlint` pass on the
      edited `test.yml`.
